title: 12 Principles of Animation (Official Full Series)
author: AlanBeckerTutorials
why: Canonical 12 principles with concrete timing logic (0-10 in-betweens change a head turn's meaning; arcs = constant X + eased Y; ones vs twos); the shared vocabulary for every keyframe and host-animation decision.

title: The #1 Skill All Animators Need
author: Ben Marriott
why: Applies anticipation (and a tour of all 12 principles) to abstract motion-graphics shapes, e.g. a 3-frame hold-key wind-up before a move; makes plain UI/shape moves read as energetic instead of robotic.

title: How to Keyframe Like a Pro! (Animation process for any software)
author: Alex Grigg // Animation for Anyone
why: Pose-to-pose order a pro uses: storytelling poses, then extremes (anticipation/overshoot/settle), then breakdowns, then spacing; a repeatable method for animating the host and any hero move.

title: Main principles of Logo Animation
author: Motion Design School
why: Shows each principle on real logo animations (overlapping letter offsets vs linear sequential reveals, arcs, volume-preserving squash/stretch); direct rules for channel idents and logo stings.

title: This Animation Technique Works Every Time
author: Ben Marriott
why: Match cuts for motion graphics: match subject or carry motion direction/speed across the cut, with breakdowns of real scene changes; cheap transitions that look expensive.

title: Why Your Motion Design Looks Cheap (5 Fixes In After Effects)
author: Stephan Zammit
why: Five studio habits: continuous flow that keeps content upright and legible while it moves, the kinetic cut that hides a scene switch at peak velocity, strategic 2D-to-3D, reactive environments, variable-weight type; each fixes a visible 'cheap' tell.

title: 10 Underrated Motion Design Techniques I LOVE
author: Ben Marriott
why: Finishing touches with exact values (gate weave = wiggle(12,3) on an adjustment layer + 101% scale, 12 fps posterized effects layer, choker to round edges); quick ways to add tactile character.

title: Master SaaS Motion Graphics in 30 Minutes (After Effects)
author: TomsProject
why: Full SaaS promo build with stated craft rules: keep continuous camera motion, offset elements instead of simultaneous entrances, match cuts between UI scenes, button presses go darker and inward (not bigger/lighter).

title: 5 Essential Type Animations in After Effects
author: Ben Marriott
why: Type that must be read should move little and deliberately: short travel with strong ease-out, subtle 104%->100% scale settle, masked reveals; restrained title motion that reads as premium.

title: 5 Tips for Amazing Storyboards | Motion Design & Animation
author: Ben Marriott
why: Thumbnail alternatives before animating (cheapest place to fix ideas), plan transitions between boards, worked example from a finished piece; fits our storyboard-first rule.

title: Style Frames for Motion Design
author: ECAbrams
why: How to choose which moments become style frames (establishing shot, end/CTA, peak action, world changes, key interactions) from a beat outline; decides what to design before generation.

title: How to Create Amazing Style Frames for Motion Design
author: Ben Marriott
why: Mood board to frame: solve values in greyscale first for contrast and focus, then build a controllable global palette; frames that already read before any motion.

title: Ultimate Guide to Camera Movement — Every Camera Movement Technique Explained [The Shot List Ep6]
author: StudioBinder
why: What each move means (push-in = emphasis/realisation, pull-out = reveal/isolation, dolly zoom, tracking, whip) so AE camera moves are chosen for meaning, not decoration.

title: How to Use Walter Murch's Eye Trace to "Direct the Eye" with Cinematic Editing
author: StudioBinder
why: Eye trace: the three levers that steer the viewer's eye (motion, position where the eye already is, colour), analysed shot by shot; the rule behind readable fast cutting and focal-point continuity between shots.

title: 6 Ways to Edit Any Scene — Essential Film & Video Editing Techniques Explained [Shot List Ep. 10]
author: StudioBinder
why: Editor's core choices (what to show, when to cut, what to cut to): cutaways, cross-cutting, centre-framed subjects for sub-2 s shots, J/L split edits, montage, cutting on action; the cut grammar for scene flow.

title: How to edit SO good your viewers get addicted to your videos
author: Learn By Leo
why: YouTube editing as attention design: when to use A-roll vs B-roll vs motion graphics, change the visual every few seconds without overloading, animate what is hard to film; the retention logic behind each edit choice.

title: Pacing in Film Editing: Techniques Every High-End Editor Must Know
author: Inside The Edit
why: High-end editor's pacing framework: five questions to plan a scene's tempo and its changes, and the four drivers of pace (cut rate, on-screen action speed, subject distance from camera, camera movement incl. crash zooms).

title: The MKBHD Method™ For Editing High Quality Videos
author: The Studio
why: Top tech channel's editors explain real decisions: re-cutting a slow intro, graphics landing exactly on the spoken word (no half-second lag), music beds under 20-30 s, whooshes sized to on-screen mass and easing.

title: 3 Sound Design Secrets That Feel Like CHEATING
author: Herman Huang
why: Layer whooshes across frequency bands for weight, carve a mid pocket in music for dialogue, keep one coherent SFX palette, reverse the song start as a riser and end on a reverb tail of the last beat.

title: The ONLY 3 Sound Effects You Need to Tell Any Story
author: Tim Runia
why: When to use whooshes (heavy vs light vs wind), risers (tension before reveals, into a smash cut to silence) and impacts; a decision table for scoring transitions and hero moments.

title: How video editors cut MUSIC for perfect timing.
author: Standard Story Company
why: Fit stock music to the edit: place the drop where speech ends and B-roll starts, loop bars to extend, cut on beats, pull the bed about 12 dB under VO; music that feels scored to the video.

title: The Role of Audio in Motion Design
author: ECAbrams
why: Same loop, different audio, different meaning; pick the music first and engineer beats into the motion, use ambience to imply a whole place with few drawn elements.

title: How VOX breaks the Digital Feel with Motion Graphics
author: Chris Moran
why: Why Vox-style explainers feel tactile: roughened edges and halftone textures, a repeatable screen treatment for screenshots with guided camera drift, consistent edge blur that pulls the eye to centre; useful for screen-recording-heavy tech explainers.

title: The Principles of Motion Design
author: Jess Riley (Envato Tuts+)
why: Design principles (hierarchy, balance and tension, contrast, negative space, repetition and rhythm) and the five animation principles that matter most in motion design, as a text lesson.

title: 10 Tiny Typography Decisions That Make Motion Graphics Feel Designed
author: School of Motion
why: Ten concrete type decisions for moving frames: decide the first read (squint test), extra room around key words, fit copy before styling, line breaks by meaning, check type on the real background, tie type to the motion.

title: Timed Text Style Guide: Subtitle Timing Guidelines
author: Netflix
why: Frame-exact rules for timing on-screen text to audio and cuts: in on the first audio frame, out about 0.5 s after speech, 2-frame minimum gaps, snap to or stay 12 frames clear of shot changes, minimum durations.

title: Executing UX Animations: Duration and Motion Characteristics
author: Page Laubheimer (Nielsen Norman Group)
why: Research-backed UI durations: about 100 ms for feedback, 200-300 ms for larger screen changes, 100-500 ms overall, ease-out as the default with ease-in only for exits; keeps animated UI in promos feeling like a real product.

title: Motion
author: IBM Carbon Design System
why: Productive vs expressive motion with each curve given as cubic-bezier AND After Effects influence (e.g. productive standard = outgoing 20%, incoming 62%), plus duration tokens 70-700 ms scaled by distance and size; drop-in values for product UI moves.

title: Tips and techniques (IBM Design Language: Animation)
author: IBM Design
why: Concrete motion-graphics rules: hand the focal point off seamlessly, single-axis camera moves feel confident, inverse complexity (dense designs get small motion), animate swatch colours not opacity, grow strokes from zero instead of crossfading.

title: Creating Usability with Motion: The UX in Motion Manifesto
author: Issara Willenskomer
why: The 12 principles of UI motion (easing, offset and delay, parenting, transformation, value change, masking, overlay, cloning, obscuration, parallax, dimensionality, dolly and zoom), each with when to use it; the grammar for animating product UI.

title: Animate with springs (WWDC23)
author: Apple
why: Apple's spring model in designer terms (duration + bounce instead of mass/stiffness, continuous velocity vs linear and bezier, when bounce fits); the basis for Apple-like UI motion.

title: An Introduction to Logo Animation Principles
author: Drew Taylor (Underbelly)
why: Logo animation planning rules: one clear message, 1-6 s length, keep motion contained in frame, never add elements the logo lacks, choose metaphor vs neutral vs illustrated story, then ease/arc/squash/anticipation/staging.

title: The Rule of Six – Walter Murch
author: Walter Murch (excerpt from In the Blink of an Eye, UC Berkeley iSchool)
why: Murch's own ranking for judging a cut (emotion 51%, story 23%, rhythm 10%, eye-trace 7%, 2D plane 5%, 3D space 4%) and the rule to sacrifice from the bottom up; a decision order for every cut.
